title: How Perceived Social, Emotional, and Behavioral Skills Differ Across the Life Span
review_rationale: SEB skills are the central constructs in an empirical cross-sectional investigation of age and gender differences across the life span.
review_evidence: [p. 2, PDF p.2, Briefly Introducing SEB Skills] The paper explicitly adopts the BESST/SEB framework and distinguishes skill capacities from typical personality traits. || [p. 4, PDF p.4, Overview of the Present Research, RQ1-RQ3] The research questions concern age gradients in SEB domains/facets and gender differences in those gradients.
quantitative_scope_rationale: One cross-sectional study. Extract only the participants not linked to the historical Internet sample D (0053d); do not treat age-range analyses as independent samples or enter age correlations. Sample/matrix IDs are assigned only after this resolved eligibility assessment.
meta_rationale: The main study measures skill capacity with the standard 192-item BESSI and supplies usable zero-order correlations and original item data. The declared overlap with Soto et al. (2022) is resolved for extraction by excluding the 596 linked Internet sample D records already represented by 0053d; historical data remain unchanged. The remaining 30,719 records provide a nonduplicated quantitative contribution.
meta_evidence: [p. 5, PDF p.5, Participants and Procedure; Measures] Participants rate their capacity to enact behaviors on the standard 192-item BESSI, using a 1-5 response scale; partial reuse of Soto et al. (2022), Study 3, is explicitly disclosed. || [p. 6, PDF p.6, Table 1 and note] Table 1 reports zero-order domain correlations for all 31,315 participants separately from covariate-adjusted correlations. || [p. 16, PDF p.16, Data Availability Statement] Data and analysis code are identified at OSF 7asgp. User-supplied local originals were inspected without executing author code. || [Local source comparison: 0 Working data file - Copycmn2.sav and d0053d.xlsx; source checksums in extraction/0150/source_manifest.csv] Cross-file verification links 596 old 0053d Case IDs to unique H-prefixed IDs in the new dataset, all agreeing on age and gender; 590 agree on all 192 items and six on 191 items. Exclusion is by linked record ID, not by approximate response matching.
